title: Bounded Counter Hook with Step & Clamp Constraints
problemStatement: Implement `createCounter({ min, max, initial, step })` with `increment()`, `decrement()`, `reset()`, and `setValue(val)` ensuring the value is strictly clamped between `min` and `max`.
interviewTrap: Failing to clamp the initial value or direct setValue input leads to invalid boundary violations in child consumers.

testCases.name: Increments and decrements within bounds
testCases.testFn: const c = createCounter({ min: 0, max: 10, initial: 0, step: 5 }); return c.increment();

testCases.name: Clamps strictly at maximum threshold
testCases.testFn: const c = createCounter({ min: 0, max: 10, initial: 8, step: 5 }); return c.increment();

testCases.name: Resets cleanly to initial value
testCases.testFn: const c = createCounter({ min: 0, max: 10, initial: 2 }); c.setValue(9); c.reset(); return c.value;

interviewCrossQuestions.question: How should state clamps (min, max, step) be enforced in reusable custom hooks?
interviewCrossQuestions.answer: By creating bounded setter functions that enforce constraints before calling the underlying state updater: `Math.min(max, Math.max(min, nextValue))`. Exposing bounded modifiers (`increment`, `decrement`, `set(val)`) guarantees the component state can never violate domain invariant boundaries.
interviewCrossQuestions.whyAsked: Tests custom hook encapsulation and state invariant enforcement.

realWorldUseCases.description: Quantity steppers that enforce inventory limits (`max: item.stock`) and minimum purchase limits (`min: 1`).
realWorldUseCases.codeSnippet: const { count, increment, decrement } = useCounter({ min: 1, max: stock, step: 1 });

howToExplain.opening: Custom hooks encapsulate state transitions behind bounded modifier functions, guaranteeing domain constraints are never violated.
keyPoints: Clamps values between min and max bounds.
Enforces single source of truth for business logic.
howToExplain.closingImpression: Encapsulating constraints inside custom hooks prevents UI components from duplicating validation logic.
analogies: A thermostat: you can press up or down, but the device physically clamps the temperature between 50°F and 90°F to protect the furnace.

commonMistakes.mistake: Allowing external callers to pass raw unclamped numbers to set().
commonMistakes.why: Allows callers to bypass min/max invariants.
commonMistakes.correct: Clamp values inside the set() method as well.

followUpDeepDive.question: How do you handle floating point rounding issues in stepped counters (e.g. 0.1 + 0.2)?
followUpDeepDive.answer: Use integer arithmetic (scale up by power of 10) or format using `Number(val.toFixed(precision))` to avoid IEEE 754 precision artifacts like `0.30000000000000004`.
